claim: FSDP FULL_SHARD unshards parameters via all-gather before the forward, reshards after it, all-gathers again before backward, reshards after backward, and reduce-scatters gradients after backward — so a full-shard step performs two all-gathers and one reduce-scatter per wrapped unit, not one all-reduce per step.
stance_target: the repo's claim that FSDP's communication volume is a per-layer all-gather/reduce-scatter pattern rather than DDP's single per-step all-reduce
quoted_support: FULL_SHARD: Parameters, gradients, and optimizer states are sharded. For the parameters, this strategy unshards (via all-gather) before the forward, reshards after the forward, unshards before the backward computation, and reshards after the backward computation. For gradients, it synchronizes and shards them (via reduce-scatter) after the backward computation.

claim: SHARD_GRAD_OP unshards parameters before the forward but does not reshard them until after backward, so parameters stay gathered between passes — the milder sharding mode that trades memory for fewer all-gathers.
stance_target: whether a milder FSDP mode could reduce communication on a slow fabric
quoted_support: SHARD_GRAD_OP: Gradients and optimizer states are sharded during computation, and additionally, parameters are sharded outside computation. For the parameters, this strategy unshards before the forward, does not reshard them after the forward, and only reshards them after the backward computation.

claim: FSDP's NO_SHARD strategy is DDP-equivalent — parameters, gradients and optimizer states replicated, gradients synchronized by all-reduce — confirming that DDP is exactly the zero-sharding end of the FSDP dial.
stance_target: the repo's framing of DDP and FSDP as two ends of one dial
quoted_support: NO_SHARD: Parameters, gradients, and optimizer states are not sharded but instead replicated across ranks similar to PyTorch's DistributedDataParallel API. For gradients, this strategy synchronizes them (via all-reduce) after the backward computation.

claim: HYBRID_SHARD applies FULL_SHARD within a node and replicates parameters across nodes, reducing communication volume because the expensive all-gathers and reduce-scatters stay intra-node — the standard mitigation for a slow inter-node link, which presupposes a fast intra-node tier.
stance_target: the claim that FSDP's cost model assumes a fast local domain; on a flat 5-GPU PCIe fabric there is no intra-node fast tier to confine the collectives to
quoted_support: HYBRID_SHARD: Apply FULL_SHARD within a node, and replicate parameters across nodes. This results in reduced communication volume as expensive all-gathers and reduce-scatters are only done within a node, which can be more performant for medium-sized models.

claim: FSDP constrains frozen parameters: with use_orig_params=False each FSDP instance must manage parameters that are all frozen or all non-frozen; with use_orig_params=True mixing is supported but discouraged because it causes higher-than-expected gradient memory usage.
stance_target: the repo's Memory Grafting plan — frozen Engram tables inside a sharded run need their own all-frozen FSDP unit, not a mixed unit
scope_conditions: PyTorch 2.13 FSDP; frozen parameters; use_orig_params flag
quoted_support: FSDP has some constraints when freezing parameters. For use_orig_params=False, each FSDP instance must manage parameters that are all frozen or all non-frozen. For use_orig_params=True, FSDP supports mixing frozen and non-frozen parameters, but it's recommended to avoid doing so to prevent higher than expected gradient memory usage.

claim: FSDP's backward_prefetch=BACKWARD_PRE holds the current parameters, the next set of parameters and the current gradients in memory at peak — the most overlap costs the most memory, which is the trade-off that makes full-shard FSDP's memory advantage smaller than the naive M/N estimate.
stance_target: the repo's claim that FSDP's memory saving is not a clean 1/N of model state
scope_conditions: PyTorch 2.13 FSDP; BackwardPrefetch.BACKWARD_PRE (default) vs BACKWARD_POST vs None
quoted_support: BACKWARD_PRE: This enables the most overlap but increases memory usage the most. This prefetches the next set of parameters before the current set of parameters' gradient computation. This overlaps the next all-gather and the current gradient computation, and at the peak, it holds the current set of parameters, next set of parameters, and current set of gradients in memory.

claim: limit_all_gathers (default True) is a rate limiter that caps GPU memory from gathered parameters to two consecutive FSDP instances' worth — the mechanism that keeps FSDP's transient all-gather buffers bounded.
stance_target: how much transient memory FSDP needs on a 64 GB card
quoted_support: limit_all_gathers (bool) - If True, then FSDP explicitly synchronizes the CPU thread to ensure GPU memory usage from only two consecutive FSDP instances (the current instance running computation and the next instance whose all-gather is prefetched).

claim: FSDP cannot run the forward pass of a submodule contained in an FSDP instance, because the submodule's parameters are sharded but the submodule itself is not an FSDP instance and so never all-gathers them — a concrete wrapping constraint for a model with frozen Engram tables bolted onto a sharded backbone.
stance_target: the implementation constraints on the repo's planned frozen-Engram + sharded-backbone model
quoted_support: FSDP does not support running the forward pass of a submodule that is contained in an FSDP instance. This is because the submodule's parameters will be sharded, but the submodule itself is not an FSDP instance, so its forward pass will not all-gather the full parameters appropriately.
